changes: Prefer verified upgrades during setup, while preserving working customer changes.
Inspect installed packages separately from running application evidence.
Save version, upgrade, verification and temporary exception records.
Keep release notes and upgrade instructions available to people and agents.
Correct shared recording privacy guidance; retain existing consent and masking choices.
upgrade: Read the upgrades guide and inspect the existing app, source, environment and repository instructions.
Run o11 upgrade plan in each application. Use the verified server release, not an unverified latest tag.
Update the command tool and SDK with the permitted installation method when the change is straightforward.
Review custom changes, event meaning, capture privacy and every routine using shared tracking.
Keep pending events and receipts, stable IDs, existing sources, credentials and disabled settings.
Verify the deployed app, real processed activity, matching and excluded examples, then save the setup record.
release.recovery: Restore the previous dependency and app commit after checking service support. Keep pending delivery IDs. Sent messages, deleted history and newly collected data cannot be undone by reinstalling a package.

support.exceptions: Keep a working older installation temporarily with a reason, owner, next action and review date. Recheck within 30 days; a review date never stops capture automatically.
support.enforcement: Advisory. No version-based rejection of existing tracking or automatic customer messaging changes.
support.scope: Newer releases receive fixes. Older installations receive upgrade help; no indefinite promise to backport fixes. Retirement requires a published notice and at least 180 days, except a separately reviewed urgent security response.

limitations: Release requirements do not prove source access, deployment, history coverage, recording consent, worker health or contact permission.
